title: CCGSC thread-pool-admin page config
description: JSON Schema 2020-12 for the config jsonb of one pool_config_version row whose page = 'thread-pool-admin'. Covers the re-run percentage, the 4 tamper measures with their parameters, the workers-per-tab min/max/auto settings, P2P enabled (default true), dew enabled with its window in seconds, the metrics on/off switches and keep_last. This document is the authority: every Save is validated against it (WWPP-R40.2). The matching PostgreSQL DDL is pool_config.sql.
$comment: Header: WO-HC-SCH-01 (hc, vostro, cmdc deepseek-v4-pro) - config storage schema, tmp only. Work order author: Claude Opus 5.5 head, 2026-11-17. Implemented by hermes MiniMax-M3, 2026-11-17. Truth input: F:/tmp/hcwork/ctx_rows_R37_R40.md rows WWPP-R38.6, WWPP-R38.7, WWPP-R40.2 and owner rule R-97. Status: tmp only, draft - not deployed, no database was contacted. Guardrails honoured: only this file and pool_config.sql were written; no DB connection; no network. END footer: the last key is x_end. T91 / R42.8, Codex, 2026-11-20: optional shared Redis settings; credentials are environment-only.

tp.gen.enabled.description: Master switch; off stops new task leasing in this pool. (WWPP-R27.1)

tp.gen.name.description: Display name shown in nav, monitors and API responses. (WWPP-R38.5)

tp.gen.fetch_mode.description: Same-device fetch mode: leader tab per device or every tab on its own; inefficient pool use always warns. (WWPP-R22.1, WWPP-R23.2)

tp.gen.shareable.description: Lets a developer mark outputs shareable; the admin may disable it for the pool. (WWPP-R23.4)

tp.gen.group_by.description: Default task partitioning key applied when the developer gives none. (WWPP-R32.2)

tp.wrk.per_tab.description: Compute web worker threads per tab; auto means logical cores minus one, otherwise 1 to 4. (WWPP-R29.4)

tp.wrk.min.description: Lowest number of compute workers the pool allows per tab. (WWPP-R29.4)

tp.wrk.max.description: Highest number of compute workers per tab; the server admin may raise it where more cores exist. (WWPP-R29.4, WWPP-R23.1)

tp.wrk.owner.description: Workers per tab on owner nodes. (WWPP-R10.4, WWPP-R29.4)

tp.wrk.phone_battery.description: Workers per tab while the phone runs on battery. (WWPP-R30.2)

tp.wrk.phone_charging.description: Workers per tab while charging with the screen on. (WWPP-R30.2)

tp.wrk.phone_stop.description: Work stops below this battery level. (WWPP-R30.2)

tp.gd.cpu.description: Contributor CPU effort profile the server asks for. (WWPP-R30.1)

tp.gd.backoff.description: Drops worker effort only when the device is very very busy. (WWPP-R30.1)

tp.gd.battery.description: Applies the phone battery and heat rules where the device supports them. (WWPP-R30.1)

tp.gd.memory.description: Upper memory bound asked of each worker, in MiB. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R30.1)

tp.gd.hidden_tab.description: Deliberately off: hidden and background tabs must keep working, never pause. (WWPP-R30.1, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.gpu.enabled.description: Allows jobs to declare cpu, gpu or gpu-preferred tasks in this pool. (WWPP-R33.1)

tp.gpu.max_slots_per_tab.description: Maximum concurrent GPU leases per contributor tab.

tp.gpu.on_battery_allowed.description: Allows GPU leases on phone and laptop tabs while they are on battery.

tp.gpu.time_limit.description: Maximum runtime of one GPU task, in seconds. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R33.1)

tp.gpu.memory_limit.description: Maximum GPU memory one task may request, in MiB. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R33.1)

tp.gpu.charging_only.description: GPU tasks are eligible only while the device is charging. (WWPP-R33.1)

tp.sch.bounded_queue.description: Caps the admitted queue depth; the queue never grows without limit. (WWPP-R32.5)

tp.sch.rejection.description: What happens when the bounded queue is full. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it; reject-429 is the proposal. (WWPP-R25.3)

tp.sch.priority_high.description: Lets the admin allow the high priority class in this pool. (WWPP-R25.2)

tp.sch.fair_share.description: Shares pool capacity fairly between developers. (WWPP-R32.5)

tp.sch.batch_size.description: Default task batch size handed to a device class. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R34.1)

tp.sch.small_task.description: Tasks below this size raise an efficiency warning on all four surfaces. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R24.4)

tp.ver.hash_check.description: Tamper measure 1 of 4: verifies artifact and input SHA-256 on every load, including IndexedDB cache hits. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R37.1b)

tp.ver.rerun_percent.description: Tamper measure 2 of 4: percentage of accepted results re-run on another worker, exact hashes only; 0 % turns the measure off. Developer-led inside the admin allowance. (WWPP-R35.1, WWPP-R37.1b)

tp.ver.signed_envelope.description: Tamper measure 3 of 4: server signs each envelope with Ed25519 over job and task ids, artifact and input hashes and the lease. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R37.1b)

tp.ver.canary.description: Tamper measure 4 of 4: schedules hidden known-answer tasks to test worker trustworthiness. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R37.1b)

tp.ver.canary_warn.description: Reputation score at or below which the worker is warned. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.ver.canary_bar.description: Reputation score at or below which the worker is barred from tasks. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.ver.canary_ban.description: Reputation score at or below which the worker is banned. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.ver.reputation_recovery.description: A ban is lifted by admin review; there is no automatic recovery. (WWPP-R37.1, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.ver.mode.description: (a) server mechanisms plus developer policy, or (b) developer only with results labelled unverified. (WWPP-R24.1)

tp.ver.k_of_n.description: Independent checks that must agree before a result counts as verified. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R24.1)

tp.ver.local_after_download.description: Lets developers verify results locally after download. (WWPP-R24.1)

tp.ver.evidence.description: (a) server minimal: security log plus SHA-256 of every accepted result, or (b) everything opt-in. (WWPP-R35.2)

tp.ver.chain.description: Per-job hash chain written by the server; built and tested even while off. (WWPP-R26.2)

tp.ver.merkle.description: Adds periodic Merkle roots over the tips of job chains. (WWPP-R22.3)

tp.ver.chain_authority.description: (a) admin global Merkle on/off with developer raise-only, or (b) developer free choice inside the allowance. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R23.3)

tp.p2p.enabled.description: Hash-addressed sharing of server-published artifacts and inputs; results always go to the server. Default ON everywhere until tested; the admin may switch it off. (WWPP-R36.2, WWPP-R36.2-RES)

tp.p2p.peer_scope.description: Which peers may serve artifacts: same device, same phone, same LAN or very close proximity. (WWPP-R9.1)

tp.p2p.task_handoff.description: Historical P2P scope kept as a setting; not an active peer data flow. (WWPP-R9.1, WWPP-R36.2)

tp.p2p.result_relay.description: Historical P2P scope kept as a setting; results are never relayed over P2P. (WWPP-R9.1, WWPP-R36.2, WWPP-R39.1)

tp.p2p.rtt_probe.description: Uses round-trip time in peer ordering once the probe exists. (WWPP-R14.1)

tp.p2p.fallback.description: Falls back to server or CDN when no peer can serve the artifact. (WWPP-R36.2)

tp.dew.enabled.description: Offline leases with signed receipts so a tab may submit results later. (WWPP-R36.2)

tp.dew.window_seconds.description: How long a signed dew receipt stays valid, in seconds; the default 86400 s is the 24 h window. (WWPP-R36.2)

tp.dew.late_policy.description: (a) archived lease id and attempt match, (b) accept only if no other attempt reported, (c) drop after re-lease. (WWPP-R13.2)

tp.dew.max_attempts.description: Attempts allowed for one task before it fails. (WWPP-R32.9)

tp.dew.job_policy.description: What the job does when a task cannot complete. (WWPP-R32.9)

tp.dew.quarantine.description: Worker crashes before a poison task is quarantined. (WWPP-R32.9)

tp.dew.dead_letter.description: Keeps late results that arrive after the job ended, with no second credit. (WWPP-R32.9)

tp.met.light.description: Light metrics: per-feature timings and counters in one PostgreSQL metrics table; disabled intervals are recorded, never fabricated. (WWPP-R37.2)

tp.met.detail.description: How much per-feature detail the metrics table keeps. Default TBD: the owner has not decided it. (WWPP-R37.2)

tp.met.benchmark.description: Heavy thesis benchmark harness for owner-started thesis runs beside the MVP. (WWPP-R37.2)

cfg.keep_last.description: Number of config versions kept for this admin page; the count is itself an admin setting. Mirrored in pool_config_retention.keep_last. (WWPP-R38.7)

cfg.reason_required.description: Each Save records who, when, what changed and why. (WWPP-R38.6)

cfg.pin_name.description: Optional admin-named pin, for example a thesis run; the name is unique per page. (WWPP-R38.7)

redis.memory.mode.description: T91 / R42.8: shared Redis cap mode; always noeviction.

redis.memory.dynamic_percent.description: Percent of Linux MemAvailable, clamped to 1-4 GiB.

redis.persistence.mode.description: AOF every second or existing Redis snapshot save rules only.

x_notes: tp.wrk.min must not exceed tp.wrk.max: JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare two sibling numbers, so this cross-field rule is enforced by the pool_config_guard_version() trigger in pool_config.sql.
The dew window is expressed in seconds (86400 s = the 24 h owner default) as the work order requires; pool_config.sql keeps the same unit in the DB check.
A property without a default is a value the owner has not decided yet; it is marked TBD in its description and must be supplied explicitly on Save.
The re-run measure is switched off with the value 0 %; it has no separate on/off switch, matching WWPP-R35.1.
Defaults listed here are the proposal carried by the admin manual source ADMIN_MANUALS_SOURCE.md and the design draft; the owner keeps the final say.

x_id_mapping.note: The admin manual source ADMIN_MANUALS_SOURCE.md is the UI list; this table maps the ids whose schema key differs from the manual id, so the app and the database agree on one name.
x_id_mapping.tp.dew.window: tp.dew.window_seconds - the manual shows hours, the schema stores seconds as the work order requires (default 86400 s = 24 h).
x_id_mapping.tp.cfg.retention: cfg.keep_last - the manual label is Version retention; the schema key is keep_last as the work order requires (default 10).
x_id_mapping.tp.cfg.pin: cfg.pin_name - the pin name itself lives in pool_config_version.pinned_name; this key carries the admin-named pin in the page config.
x_id_mapping.tp.cfg.reason: cfg.reason_required - the reason text lives in pool_config_version.reason; this key says whether a Save may omit it.
x_id_mapping.tp.cfg.rollback: not a stored value - rollback is the pool_config_rollback() function in pool_config.sql, it creates a new audited version.

x_tamper_measures.1: tp.ver.hash_check - hash check on every load, including IndexedDB cache hits (WWPP-R37.1)
x_tamper_measures.2: tp.ver.rerun_percent - random re-run percentage, 0 % switches the measure off (WWPP-R35.1)
x_tamper_measures.4: tp.ver.canary - canary known-answer tasks plus the reputation thresholds (WWPP-R37.1)
x_tamper_measures.configurable_on: the admin pages, on and off with parameters each (WWPP-R37.1b)
